findings.description: The reconciliation success criteria require a REST /get_user_trades query to detect missing trades, but the contract does not specify what happens when that REST call fails or times out. Fail-closed behavior demands that a query failure be treated as missing-trade evidence (reconciliation fails, latch stays set), but this is nowhere stated.

evidence.quote: No missing trades over the last `reconcile_trade_lookback_sec` (default: 300s) as determined by REST `/get_user_trades` query.
evidence.context: Reconciliation success criteria bullet; no handling of REST call failure defined

findings.proposed_fix: Add: 'If the REST /get_user_trades call fails or times out, reconciliation MUST fail and the latch MUST remain set (fail-closed).' Add a corresponding AT for this path.

findings.description: 'Deterministic reconstruction (preferred; no persistence)' uses advisory language for a safety-critical startup property. If a system legally persists stale latch state and that state is clear, the RESTART_RECONCILE_REQUIRED latch is never set and false-safe opens become possible after restart—directly violating the section goal.

evidence.context: Section heading treats no-persistence as a preference, not a requirement

findings.proposed_fix: Replace 'preferred; no persistence' with 'REQUIRED; persistence is prohibited'. The startup rule on line 20 already uses MUST; the heading must match.

findings.description: Five reason codes (WS_BOOK_GAP_RECONCILE_REQUIRED, WS_TRADES_GAP_RECONCILE_REQUIRED, WS_DATA_STALE_RECONCILE_REQUIRED, INVENTORY_MISMATCH_RECONCILE_REQUIRED, SESSION_TERMINATION_RECONCILE_REQUIRED) have no AT that tests the trigger event that SETS the latch. ATs only test behavior after the latch is already set (AT-010, AT-011, AT-402, AT-110). The set-trigger side of each non-RESTART reason code is unproven.

evidence.context: Allowed values list; no corresponding set-trigger AT for any WS or session code

findings.proposed_fix: Add at least one AT per non-RESTART trigger class (WS gap, WS stale, inventory mismatch, session termination) proving that the relevant event both sets open_permission_blocked_latch=true and populates the correct reason code.

findings.description: AT-411 only tests F1/EvidenceChain isolation under 'no reconcile-class triggers are active'. The Hard rule (line 44) is unconditional: these codes MUST NOT appear regardless of whether reconcile triggers are simultaneously active. There is no AT covering the concurrent case (reconcile trigger active AND cert/evidence failure), leaving the unconditional hard rule unproven.

evidence.quote: Given: runtime binding cert is missing/stale/FAIL OR (`EvidenceChainState != GREEN` and `enforced_profile != CSP`), and no reconcile-class triggers are active.
evidence.context: AT-411 given clause restricts to no-reconcile-trigger scenario only

findings.proposed_fix: Add an AT: Given a reconcile-class trigger is active AND cert/evidence failure is also present, then open_permission_reason_codes MUST NOT contain any runtime-binding or EvidenceChain code; only the reconcile-class code(s) appear.

findings.description: The Semantics section (lines 7-9) states only that OPEN intents MUST be blocked while latch is true, implying latch-clear = opens allowed. AT-011 introduces an additional PolicyGuard dependency ('opens may proceed only if PolicyGuard computes TradingMode::Active') that is not stated in Semantics. An implementer reading only Semantics would not know the latch is necessary-but-not-sufficient for opens.

evidence.quote: opens may proceed only if PolicyGuard computes `TradingMode::Active`
evidence.context: AT-011 Then clause; this PolicyGuard dependency is absent from the Semantics section

findings.proposed_fix: Add to Semantics: 'Latch clearance is necessary but not sufficient for OPEN permission; PolicyGuard must independently compute TradingMode::Active before OPEN intents are dispatched.'
